$comment: Arceus Heartbeat Scheduling Engine configuration. All values can be overridden by env vars prefixed ARCEUS_HEARTBEAT_*
$comment_concurrency: maxConcurrentBeats = global ceiling across ALL tenants (safety valve so 20 tenants × 2-per-company can't open 40 Azure requests). maxConcurrentBeatsPerCompany = per-tenant slot pool — one company's hung beat cannot starve another's. Total in-flight = min(global, sum of per-company active). Lowered from 8/2 to 4/1 under multi-tenant load: gpt-5.4-mini Azure deployment was hitting TPM saturation at 4+ concurrent beats, manifesting as `totalTokens: 0` silent stalls rather than 429s. Bump these back up after either (a) Azure quota increase, or (b) deployment split (chat vs beats).
$comment_roleIntervals: Minimum gap between same-role beats. Halved across the board for fail-fast: when an SSE-watchdog stall kills a beat at 60s, the role waits roleInterval ms before retrying. Old values made retries take 60-120s extra after a stall; new values cut that to 20-30s. Per-company concurrency cap (1) prevents this from increasing Azure TPM pressure — only ONE beat per tenant fires at a time regardless of role intervals.
$comment_beatTimeoutMs: Overall wall-clock ceiling for one beat. 15min→10min→15min: lowered when stalls were undetectable and this cap was the only defense; raised back once the stall stack landed (BEAT_STALL silence nudge ~2.5min, reasoning-stall 6min, stranded-run sweeper releasing claims). Only productive beats reach this ceiling now — post-stall-fix telemetry showed working developer beats guillotined at 10min before their serialize phase. The wrap-up nudge in prompts/llm.ts fires 2min before the cap so beats checkpoint instead of dying mid-edit.
